description: Remote-access policy for Nuxel. OFF by default. When enabled, access is restricted to the owner console path, never to the open network.

indicator.pwa_badge: privacy/js/privacy.js renders 'REMOTE ACCESS ON' from this file's state via the daemon status API
indicator.note: If the indicator cannot be rendered, enabling remote access is refused: an invisible remote access path is not acceptable.

ssh_gadget.note: The USB gadget interface only. Binding 0.0.0.0 would expose the phone on whatever network it is joined to; the CLI refuses a wildcard bind.

serial_console.note: The CDC-ACM console is the recovery path and is never disabled by any network policy (see configs/nftables/nuxel-console-guard.nft).

forbidden: enabling remote access without the indicator
remote access over the cellular interface (rmnet0 is disabled in the firewall config)
enforcement_note: Enforced by the CLI (which refuses the forbidden states) and by the firewall interface policy (configs/nftables/nuxel-firewall-config.json: usb0 is the console interface, rmnet0 is disabled). This is a userspace + nftables boundary against unprivileged apps; root can change anything and is out of scope.

wlan_ssh.listen: 0.0.0.0:22 and [::]:22, but authentication is restricted by sshd AllowUsers host CIDRs
wlan_ssh.firewall_note: The live Fedora image has no nft/iptables binary; the effective restriction is sshd AllowUsers user@CIDR plus the absence of any port-forward/NAT rule. Port 22 is not exposed to the public Internet.

usb_ssh.status: BLOCKED_KERNEL_PANIC on the live Samsung-derived 4.14.253 kernel
usb_ssh.note: CONFIG_USB_F_NCM/CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS_NCM are compiled in, but the NCM function teardown (ncm_free_inst -> misc_deregister) panicked the kernel and the watchdog rebooted the phone. No USB network transport is claimed.
